title: MacBook Neo Review: Apple's $599 Disruptor Tested

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: The arrival of the MacBook Neo in March 2026 marks Apple's most aggressive move into the budget laptop market. At $599, it's designed to kill the high-end Chromebook and dominate the student market.

sections.heading: Design and Portability
sections.content: Analysis of the ultra-portable 12-inch form factor, the return of the fanless design, and the choice of materials (recycled aluminum). Comparison to the MacBook Air M3 size.

sections.heading: Performance: The M3 Legacy
sections.content: How the M3 chip performs in 2026 for everyday tasks, browsing, and light creative work. Benchmarks against the latest Chromebook Plus models.

sections.heading: Display and Battery Life
sections.content: Review of the 12.5-inch Liquid Retina display (500 nits) and the impressive 16-hour real-world battery life that outlasts almost everything in its price bracket.

sections.heading: The Compromises
sections.content: Honest look at what you lose for $599: 8GB base RAM, limited port selection (2x USB-C), and the 720p webcam.

sections.heading: Value vs. Competition
sections.content: Comparison table: MacBook Neo vs. Samsung Galaxy Book 4 Go vs. Premium Chromebooks.

sections.heading: Where to Buy
sections.content: Affiliate section with links to Amazon for the Neo and the MacBook Air M3 as a step-up alternative.

sections.heading: Verdict
sections.content: Final score and recommendation: Who should buy this and who should save for the Air.
